analysis: The PR adds a cold-KV forecast (coldKVEstimates) fed by provider-reported telemetry (ADV-001). The forecast feeds three consumers: the fleet_snapshots sampler (fleet_sample.go:87, fleet_sample_kv.go), the memory-policy input (memory_policy_projection.go: EstimatedKVBytesPerToken), and the public ModelCapacitySnapshot (model_capacity.go patch around lines 80-145). The sampler is lock-disciplined: it captures requirements under p.mu only, copies the model index under a short r.mu.RLock, and validates each donor with its own r.mu then p.mu lease (the established order). The sampler is off the request path and keyed by provider-authored slot and model strings. ModelCapacitySnapshot instead calls coldKVEstimatesLocked(providers, "", now) under the long r.mu.RLock and uses estimates.Rate as the cold-slot rate. That is the finding above. I could not see these definitions: observedColdKVRateLocked, coldKVEstimatesLocked, coldKVRequirements.addLocked, the snapshotProviderIntoLockedEx/fillSnapshotPendingAndPool changes, and the memorypolicy and kvbudget packages. The following need a pass: whether provider-reported KV rates are clamped, whether the identity key is provider-spoofable, and whether estimates can create slot grants or weaken admission (the comment says the forecast never creates a slot grant). Also unchecked: whether the public capacity endpoint is authenticated or rate-limited, and the unseen call sites of the changed signatures. No auth, attestation, encryption, or billing paths are touched in the supplied files.

findings.detail: ModelCapacitySnapshot now calls r.coldKVEstimatesLocked(providers, "", now) inside the long r.mu.RLock section, then takes every p.mu in the same loop. The sibling fleet_sample_kv.go explicitly avoids this: it takes a short lease per donor and never holds one across a peer walk. The forecast walks peers for each model using provider-authored slot and model strings and heartbeat telemetry from ADV-001. With many connected or fake-registered providers advertising many distinct models, the cost grows roughly as providers times models, all under r.mu.RLock. A pending writer (register, disconnect, dispatch) can block behind the long reader and starve other readers. If the capacity feed is publicly reachable, a consumer or attacker can poll it to amplify this. Separately, estimates take the max rate across donors, so one provider that reports an inflated cold KV rate could shrink the public capacity numbers for that model. Fix: use the fleet_sample pattern (capture requirements, then per-donor short leases), cache the forecast with a TTL, cap per-sample work, and bound or sanity-check provider-reported rates.
findings.title: Public capacity snapshot now runs provider-fed cold-KV forecast while holding the registry read lock
